transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-11 10:00am PDT | Duration: 58 minutes | Host: Avery Park
Attendees: Avery Park, Rahul Desai, Linnea Ortiz, Diego Ramos, Priya Kapoor, Samir Kaur + open crew

Summary (auto): Monthly leadership check-in; quick updates from eng, product, people; discussion on capacity predictability and rollout speed; finalize owners for a short list of action items.

[00:00] Avery: Yeah good morning everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to keep this tight, we've got 50ish minutes, agenda's up in the doc, um quick operating radar then a few tradeoff discussions.
[00:18] Rahul: Morning. on infra i want to flag two things, first our dedicated pool variance is causing some throughput jitter for anchors customers, and second, we still have tail latency that spikes under thundering-herd patterns.
[00:33] Linnea: We also surfaced from product-side that Optimize suggestions are getting noisy for some customers, esp when batching policy flips automatically. that ties into the routing piece.
[00:46] Avery: Okay can you give the short TLDR Rahul? like what's the customer visible impact?
[00:51] Rahul: TLDR: for about 8% of requests in dedicated-small pools, 99p jumps by 60 to 120ms; it's intermittant, often correlates with background GC-ish on the orchestration nodes, maybe kernel scheduling. so customers notice occasional stutter. not a full outage but it pushes some latency-sensitive SLAs.
[01:15] Diego: quick add — i think our batching heuristics sometimes compound that, we have a batch that goes out and it waits for an extra microbatch when there's a scheduling delay so the perceived latency is longer. the new batching engine reduces that by re-evaluating cutpoints but it's not live everywhere.
[01:33] Samir: and to be clear the cost profiles are also affected; when we move to more aggressive caching the unit cost drops but warmup amplifies jitter on first requests.
[01:47] Avery: cool. high-level tradeoff then: do we prioritize rolling the new batching engine across all dedicated pools ASAP, or do we focus on routing fallback policies so that latency-sensitive traffic is routed to larger/more stable pools?
[02:00] Linnea: I lean routing first — low blast radius, we can define policy fast, good short-term mitigation while batching rollout continues.
[02:06] Rahul: Routing is good but long term we need the engine baked in — otherwise we have an ops tax. also routing adds cost because larger pools are less efficient per token.
[02:18] Avery: noted. let's try a two-track: short-term routing + immediate canary of batching engine in a subset of tenants. Diego, can you scope the canary?
[02:26] Diego: yes, i'll do a canary across 10 internal tenants and two paid customers, monitor 99p and failure rates, will look for regression in correctness. aim to start next week.
[02:36] Linnea: product will provide the test prompts and critical paths. we'll also add a playback harness so we can reproduce customer traffic shapes.
[02:44] Avery: Great. second topic, hiring — Priya?
[02:49] Priya: hiring update: recruitment funnel is ok but time-to-offer is slipping; we have open reqs for infra, platform, and two SREs. budget for Q3 allows 12 heads but we need to prioritize.
[03:01] Avery: we discussed prioritization earlier, but we need a concrete list. i want 6 priority hires this quarter that unblock throughput and reliability. Linnea, product headcount asks?
[03:11] Linnea: product asks for two data-centric PMs for Optimize and Console. the impact is high on unit economics. i'll send a one-pager with impact estimates.
[03:18] Avery: good. Priya, can you publish the slotted hires with owners by next week?
[03:23] Priya: yes, i'll have that by 2026-08-18.
[03:27] (murmur, someone drops in chat: 'can we pause for 30s for a quick demo?')
[03:33] Avery: we have time, rahul, is there a quick perf chart?
[03:36] Rahul: i've uploaded a draft perf baseline to the crew drive, link in chat. quick note — the 99p target we discussed internally of 180ms for hosted, 250ms for dedicated is still our goal but it's slipping slightly on dedicated-small.
[03:50] Diego: also FYI, canary rollout gating is manual today; ops needs a better rollback and metrics hook. i've put in a PR for automated rollback by looking at 99p and error rate thresholds but it's behind one infra change.
[04:05] Linnea: can we standardize on the observable set for rollouts? so SEs know the exact metrics they should watch.
[04:12] Samir: yes, we'll ship a rollout playbook with a standardized dashboard.
[04:16] Avery: ok that should be an action item. Samir take it.
[04:19] Samir: noted.
[04:21] [05:00] (brief pause — channel chatter about hackweek demos)
[05:12] Avery: second half — strategic bets and runway. finance says we have a 16-month runway at current burn, that assumes 12% ARR growth in the next two quarters. if growth slows we need to tighten hiring.
[05:27] Priya: on people ops we are rolling out an updated performance calibration process — minimal change to cycle but better consistency. also rolling out manager training for interviewing.
[05:38] Linnea: product roadmap — we've delayed the Evaluate feature in favor of deeper Optimize integrations. the tradeoff was because Optimize gives better near-term unit-cost wins.
[05:49] Diego: i want to push back a bit, Evaluate provides guardrails for quality, which is critical for enterprise renewals. without it, sales might struggle.
[05:58] Avery: fair. let's have product scope a phased Evaluate where MVP is a lightweight rule-based eval tool for customers, then a deeper integration after Optimize patches.
[06:10] Linnea: ok we'll slot that into Q4 planning but prepare a customer-facing MVP in Q3 if possible.
[06:18] [09:10] Audience Q: "What's our stance on private deployments and on-prem in regulated sectors?"
[09:15] Rahul: we continue to support Private with a focused package — more prescriptive on operator-run options and HSM integrations. it's higher touch but it's strategic for a subset of customers.
[09:26] Priya: sales needs a clearer checklist for security pre-sales. we should finalize the SOC2 scope addendum and an FAQ.
[09:33] Avery: action: product/security collaborate on a pre-sales checklist.
[09:36] Rahul: i'll get the security team to review.
[09:39] [12:00] (cross-talk, someone says 'KV cache', misheard as 'K-V cash')
[12:05] Diego: technical note — the KV cache compaction bug is fixed in branch but we need to validate long tails on very long sequences.
[12:17] Linnea: that's the thing customers with long context windows hit. add it to the canary test matrix.
[12:22] Diego: will do.
[12:25] [18:40] Avery: quick risk radar readout: 1) capacity predictability for Dedicated (mitigation: routing + batching canary), 2) rollout velocity (mitigation: rollout automation + standard dashboards), 3) hiring velocity (mitigation: prioritize 6 hires, tighten interview loop), 4) competitor motion — CloudAIInc launched a new managed endpoint with opaque batching settings — watch for a PR risk.
[19:06] Rahul: also legal flagged a faster RFP timeline for one enterprise deal; they want a SOC2 + encryption SLA tightener.
[19:12] Priya: we've prepped a template but will need product sign-off.
[19:19] [22:00] Linnea: lightning updates from squads: Console team shipping per-route cost breakdown next week; Optimize team iterating on quantization suggestions; Serving runtime team working on kernel selector perf gains.
[22:14] Diego: runtime team to also start a microbenchmark series for model families we'll publish internally.
[22:21] [28:46] (brief demo interruption, someone notes 'function calling is messy in one flow')
[28:55] Linnea: function-calling UX needs clarity, we'll schedule a cross-team session with SDK and DX to fix it.
[29:04] Samir: noted, will book.
[29:10] [35:00] People moment: Priya thanks the recruiting team and the folks who mentored interns last cycle. new parental leave policy update will be in the handbook next week.
[35:20] Priya: also starting a mentorship cohort pilot — signups open.
[35:27] [40:00] Q&A: "How do we decide between dedicated vs hosted for new customers?"
[40:07] Rahul: decision matrix: latency critical + data residency -> private/dedicated; heavy throughput predictable -> dedicated; casual/prototyping -> hosted. we'll formalize and publish.
[40:18] Linnea: add cost sensitivity and SLA needs to the matrix.
[40:23] Avery: ok product + sales draft decision tree and a one-pager for solutions by 2026-08-16.
[40:30] [48:00] Closing: Avery recaps owners — routing policy + canary (Diego/Rahul), hiring slots (Priya/Avery), rollout playbook + dashboards (Samir), product prioritization doc (Linnea).
[48:20] Avery: thanks everyone. reminders: hackweek demo day is 2026-08-28, submit proposals by 2026-08-18.
[48:30] Diego: will follow up on the canary plan in the crew channel.
[48:35] Linnea: i'll circulate the prioritized feature doc after a short sync with product ops.
[48:42] (meeting winds down, some applause emotes in chat)
[58:00] End of recording.

Artifacts referenced: Q3 hiring draft (link in crew drive), perf baseline spreadsheet (link in chat), routing policy doc (draft), batching engine PR (internal link), hackweek submission form.
